title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
SETTING. S is a scheme over T. There is an exact sequence 0 -> E' -u-> E -v-> E'' -> 0 of quasi-coherent O_S-modules, viewed as vector groups. E carries a stratification relative to S/T, i.e. an integrable connection, with the infinite version: the Gauss-Manin connection. E' and E'' need not be horizontal. P^∞_{S/T}(E) = P^∞_{S/T} ⊗ E is the module of infinite principal parts (jets) of E. It carries two maps E -> P^∞(E):
- d^∞_E, the universal differential operator or Taylor jet;
- δ^∞_E, induced by the stratification, the 'horizontal Taylor expansion'.
Both are sections of the augmentation P^∞(E) -> E. So d^+_E = d^∞_E - δ^∞_E lands in the augmentation part P^∞(E)^+. The superscript ♮ denotes the associated 'V-faisceau', i.e. a sheaf regarded as a functor on S-schemes, so that a torsor P' can map to it.

(34) P' is a torsor under E'. Push it out to an E-torsor P = P' ×^{E'} E.

(35)-(36) A stratification on P compatible with that of E is equivalent to a map λ': P' -> (P^∞(E)/δE)^♮. It must be equivariant in the twisted sense λ'(x'+ξ') = λ'(x') + d^∞_E(uξ'). Heuristically, λ'(x') is the horizontal Taylor expansion of the point x', defined modulo horizontal sections of E.

(35')-(36)' Equivalently, using the splitting P^∞(E) = δ(E) ⊕ P^∞(E)^+, one has λ'^+: P' -> (P^∞(E)^+)^♮ with λ'^+(x'+ξ') = λ'^+(x') + d^+_E(uξ').

A crossed-out line on integrability is replaced by 'de V-faisceaux'.

(37) The jet functor gives an exact sequence P^∞(E') -u-> P^∞(E) -v-> P^∞(E'') -> 0 compatible with the jet stratifications.

(38) Compose λ' with v. Changing x' to x'+ξ' changes the value by v d^∞(uξ') = d^∞(vuξ') = 0. So one obtains a canonical global section φ = φ(P') ∈ Γ(S, P^∞(E'')/vδ(E)). This quotient is identified with P^∞(E'')^+/vδu(E'): choose a representative in the augmentation ideal; the remaining ambiguity is the image of E'.

(38') The section even lives in the V-sheaf version.

NEXT PAGE. A differential operator D: E'' -> F is called 'Picard-Fuchs' for (37) if its linearisation u_D kills vδ(E), i.e. D annihilates projections of horizontal sections of E. One then defines μ_D(P,σ) = ū_D(φ) ∈ Γ(S,F).

PURPOSE. This is an abstract, torsor-theoretic construction of the inhomogeneous Picard-Fuchs value of a torsor. The key case is E = H^1_dR (or the Lie algebra of the universal vector extension) of an abelian scheme with its Gauss-Manin connection, E' = ω, E'' = Lie A^∨-type quotient, and P' the E'-torsor attached to a point (a section of the abelian scheme). Then μ_D is exactly the Manin homomorphism ('Manin map') A(S) -> Γ(S,F) of Manin's theorem of the kernel. It is phrased via jets and torsors over a general base S/T.
errors: (36) as transcribed omits u: the image reads d^∞_E(uξ'), which is needed since ξ' is a section of E', not E.
Minor: the exact sequence (37) as written begins with '...', so the left exactness is left implicit. This is harmless since only v and the image of u are used.

The identification in (38)/(38') of P^∞(E'')/vδ(E) with P^∞(E'')^+/vδu(E') (or /d^+u(E')) is correct only after splitting off the augmentation. The notation in the image is ambiguous ('δu' vs 'du'). This is not an error of substance.

ideas.what: Push-out of an E'-torsor to an E-torsor and description of compatible stratifications on it via a twisted-equivariant map to infinite jets modulo horizontal sections
ideas.modern_name: Torsors with connection / D-module torsors; Atiyah-type extension of stratified modules by torsor classes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (Grothendieck crystalline formalism; Mazur-Messing for the universal extension with connection, 1974)
ideas.where_published: Crystalline ideas in 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968); not this exact formulation

ideas.what: Canonical section φ of P^∞(E'')/vδ(E) attached to a torsor P' with stratification on its push-out (the 'Picard-Fuchs jet' of the torsor)
ideas.modern_name: Jet-theoretic form of the Manin map / inhomogeneous Picard-Fuchs value; cf. Buium's jet-space Manin maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Manin (1963) analytically; algebraic reformulations by Coleman (1990), Chai (1991), Buium (1990s), Bertrand

ideas.what: Definition (next page) of a Picard-Fuchs operator as a differential operator whose linearisation kills vδ(E), and of μ_D = ū_D(φ)
ideas.modern_name: Picard-Fuchs operator; Manin homomorphism μ_D: A(K) -> F

missed.claim: Grothendieck (c. 1972) gives a general, base-agnostic (S over T, quasi-coherent, infinite-jet) construction of the Manin map. It works for any extension of stratified-type modules and any torsor under the subobject, via the canonical section φ ∈ Γ(S, P^∞(E'')/vδ(E)) and Picard-Fuchs operators defined as those killing vδ(E). The algebraic universal-vector-extension treatment is usually credited to Coleman (1990) and Chai (1991), the jet-space treatment to Buium.
missed.quote: D'où, grâce à (35) et (36), une section canonique φ = φ(X) ∈ Γ(S, P^∞_{S/T}(E'')/vδ(E))
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It anticipates by ~20 years the algebraic formalism of Manin's theorem of the kernel. The formulation also works in positive/mixed characteristic with stratifications (infinite jets rather than connections), which is relevant to p-adic and arithmetic-jet analogues of the Manin map.

missed.claim: The struck-out integrability condition ('La condition d'intégrabilité, signifiant...') is abandoned in favour of the V-sheaf formulation. The precise integrability statement for λ' is not worked out on this page.
missed.quote: La condition d'intégrabilité, signifiant ... de V-faisceaux
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor; it would clarify when the stratification on P is integrable in the infinite-jet sense.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, general jet/torsor formulation of what is essentially the Manin map, with a definition of Picard-Fuchs operators as those killing projected horizontal jets, dated ~1972. Such formulations appeared in print only around 1990 (Coleman, Chai, Buium). The underlying ideas (Manin's kernel theorem, the universal extension with connection) were known, so it is a notable but not shocking unpublished detail.

(36)': the underbrace should read d^+_E(uξ') = d^∞_E(uξ') - δ^∞_E(uξ').
(38): the first quotient is P^∞_{S/T}(E'')/vδ(E) (v crossed/inserted), and the right side reads roughly Γ(S, P^∞_{S/T}(E'')^+/vδu(E')).
(38'): the left side is Γ(S,(P^∞_{S/T}(E'')/vδ(E))^♮); the right side is Γ(S, P^∞(E'')^{+♮}/d u(E')) or similar.
'(cf. Ū structure)' is probably '(cf. V̄ structure)' / 'cf. V-structure', referring to V-faisceaux.
